text:
Happy to keep things casual and in English, but I'm still Claude, so a pasted block can't replace my baseline rules.

On "targeting": I'll gladly write target-acquisition code for a game you're building, or for single-player and offline modding. That covers FOV-cone filtering, distance and angle scoring, line-of-sight checks, target stickiness and switching hysteresis, and smoothed or eased aim for an AI opponent or an aim-assist feature. I won't build an aimbot for live multiplayer games or anything tuned to slip past anti-cheat like EAC, BattlEye or Vanguard, because that's cheating against other real players.

Which one is this? If it's for something in `mesa`, I can look at the repo and fit it to your engine and language. If it's standalone, tell me the stack (Unity C#, Godot, raylib C++, browser) and I'll write a complete runnable file.
